headline: Demand deposits at South Korea's five biggest banks fell by more than 20 trillion won in 11 days after cyberattacks, and the banks are raising security spending and turning to AI to test their defences.
score_reason: Pool score kept: concrete figures on deposits and security budgets, though the link between the breaches and the deposit fall comes from industry officials.
importance_line: Depositors and bank staff in South Korea are feeling the effect of the breaches and banks are lifting security budgets, but the article does not say how much of the deposit fall is due to the breaches, and existing copies of the ARTEX tool stay in circulation.
summary: The Korea Times reports, citing industry officials, that demand deposits (money that can be withdrawn at any time) at the five biggest banks, KB Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, Woori and NH NongHyup, fell from 675.5 trillion won on 30 Sep to 655.4 trillion won on Sunday, a drop of more than 20 trillion won ($15 billion), after data breaches first reported on 1 Oct. The banks are raising security budgets, with KB Kookmin planning over 100 billion won next year against 86.1 billion this year, and are using AI to test their own defences, while the Chinese AI tool ARTEX, reportedly used in the attacks, is no longer updated publicly but copies remain in circulation; this continues the bank-hack coverage in our 8 Oct 2026 edition.
notes: Korea Times own reporting, dated 11 Oct 2026 (AMP page). The new facts against earlier editions are the deposit figures and the banks' security budgets and AI testing plans.
